decision: Would a referral program bring in customers more cheaply than the channel it replaces, and what is the most we can pay in rewards?
limitations: Ask and conversion rates are usually guesses before launch. With assumed inputs the output is a scenario; replace them with measured rates after the first period.
It models one period. The amplification figure assumes referred customers refer at the same rate as others, which is unmeasured until they do.
Referred customers get the same LTV unless you pass a measured referredLtv. Do not assume they are worth more; the 16% finding is from one bank.
Compliance flags print pointers to rules (FTC, Anti-Kickback, HIPAA); they are not a legal check. The research is mostly consumer, with no peer-reviewed B2B cash-reward study.
review: The founder or finance lead confirms LTV, the CAC being replaced and which rates are assumptions. Counsel reviews any reward involving public posts, reviews or healthcare providers before launch.
